To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the oxygen vacancy concentration is the main factor for the thermal expansion of the perovkite-type oxides, which in turn is the main factor that influences the ionic conductivity.
the ionic conductivity of mixed conducting perovksite oxides is strongly correlated with their thermal expansion coefficients.

the ionic conductivities of mixed conducting perov skite-type oxides can be estimated by the thermal expansion coefficient and that the correlation between both quantities is based on the oxygen vacancy concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new materials for solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) cathodes, which have to fulfill a number of requirements.
the development of new cathode materials for SOFCs with high ionic and electronic conductivity and low thermal expansion coefficient.

a general correlation between the oxygen vacancy concentration and the thermal expansion coefficient, which is of importance for the design of cathodes with low thermal stresses in solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) and other electrochemical devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the higher the thermal expansion coefficient, the higher is the ionic conductivity.
the higher the ionic conductivity, the higher the thermal expansion.
in the perovskites the thermal expansion coefficients are mainly influenced by the A-site cation radius and the ionic conductivity by the B-site cation radius.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the increase of the 10 ^{−6} K ^{−1} -range of TEC is accompanied by an increase of oxygen vacancy concentration and ionic conductivity, but by a decrease of the electrical conductivity of the perovksite oxides.
the increase in ionic conductivity is accompanied by an increase in thermal expansion coefficient.
the ionic conductivity increases with the thermal expansion coefficient and that the electronic conductivity is not affected by the thermal expansion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a high thermal expansion coefficient is not a necessary condition for high oxide ion conductivity in the perovskites investigated.
the thermal expansion of perovskite oxides can be used to predict the ionic conductivity in a broad range of materials.
the thermal expansion coefficient is a suitable indicator for the oxygen vacancy concentration and thus for ionic conductivity in mixed conductors.
